message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate the submission against the rubric.

C1 Introduction: mission concept, rationale, spacecraft count, users. All addressed: primary mission (coral reef monitoring via fluid lensing), why needed (bleaching), one satellite with justification, users (CSIRO, BOM, government/university funding). References cited. Good detail. Accomplished, maybe 8.

C2 Mission design: launch site/vehicle (Kourou, Vega E with rationale), orbit type and elements (SSO, 600 km, i=97.79°, COE table), manoeuvres (none except EOL), ground control (Mt Pleasant), comms frequency (STK access report, ~10 min mean, multiple passes/day), mission duration (5 years) and EOL (drag sail). STK screenshots included (Images 1,2,4,5, access table, inclination plot). Some issues: "A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" — error (should be "not desirable" or "undesirable"). Also "which – because of its verticality – maintains a significant contact" awkward. RAAN 27.33° "indicates location of launch facility" — questionable but plausible. Also the inclination plot: at 600 km, SSO inclination ~97.8°, correct. Semi-major axis 6971 km correct. Access table shows ~6 passes/day, plausible for Tasmania with near-polar orbit. Some minor errors but overall comprehensive with evidence. Accomplished range, maybe 7-8. The "very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" is a clear error. Also the claim "the satellite will be positioned at 600km and images of reef sections will be compiled daily" — fine. Also the statement about drag sail: "utilising a large surface area to ' and is suitable" — OCR artifact likely. I'd give 8.

Actually check: "The satellite must be far away enough to capture the width of the Great Barrier Reef – if daily images are to capture the entire reef" — logic slightly muddled but ok. Give 8.

C3 Conclusion: summarizes findings, notes risks (Vega E not built), specific. Adequate-to-accomplished. It's fairly brief but reaches specific conclusions tied to evidence. Give 7.

C4 Presentation: structure clear, headings, executive summary present, figures labelled? Figures have captions like "STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart" but no figure numbers ("Figure 1"). Tables not labelled with numbers. Bibliography is just URLs, not properly formatted references; uses Wikipedia as reference [6] — task says Wikipedia not accepted as proper source. That's a citation issue. In-text citations [1]-[10] match list. Some grammar issues ("a Earth observation", "It's first launch", "for the purposed of this satellite", "current owned"). Formatting inconsistent (heading levels vary: #, ##, #####). Adequate level, maybe 5. Wikipedia use is a requirement violation (R15). Give 5.

Requirements:
R1 yes (reef monitoring benefits Australia). R2 yes. R3 yes. R4 yes. R5 yes. R6 yes. R7 yes. R8 yes (none except EOL). R9 yes. R10 yes. R11 yes (STK used, plus hand calc plot). R12 partial — screenshots included, but no mention of software files included in appendix. R13 yes. R14 partial — figures have captions but no figure numbers; tables unlabelled. R15 partial — Wikipedia used as source [6].

Technical issues:
- "A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" — contradiction/error.
- Wikipedia cited as reference [6].
- RAAN 27.33° "indicates the location of the launch facility" — questionable; RAAN relates to orbit plane, not launch site directly.
- Claim "ground facility will be able to receive all new data from the previous period" unsupported.
- Drag sail section: text garbled "utilising a large surface area to '" (possibly OCR).
- Access table row numbering offset (row "----" then 1...) minor.
- Statement "sun-synchronous orbit inherently experiences significant J2 perturbations as a result of its highly polar inclination" — J2 nodal precession, fine.
- "two launch windows will occur per day" for inclination > latitude — correct.
- Mission duration: "may be lengthened though, by the addition of solar panels" — odd; solar panels are standard, not EOL extension.

Overall: solid report with good STK evidence, some errors and referencing issues.
